_comment: Skills whose trigger-probe status (`never` / `STALE`) is KNOWN and ACCEPTED, read by skills/skill-authoring/scripts/case_coverage.py's P004. Probing costs live model calls (~$0.05/probe, $6.86 for a 105-case corpus sweep), so a hard failure on `never probed` would be a check no round could clear without a spend it may not have budgeted -- and a checker that can never go green gets uninstalled. An entry silences P004 for that skill. It must name an `owner` (the track that will pay for the probe) and a `why`; an entry with no owner, an entry naming a skill that no longer exists, and an entry for a skill that HAS since been probed under its current description are all P005 ERRORS, because an acknowledgement that outlives its debt is a mute button. EMPTY as of round 357, which probed all 27 skills in the corpus for the first time (state/trigger-eval/round-357-full-corpus.{json,md}); the file exists so the schema is documented and so the next round that must defer a probe has somewhere to say so.

bounded-not-binary-witness.why: Written by round 358 (NUC-integration E). A probe is a priced live run and this program's standing convention is that E-rounds do not launch priced batches -- round 334's item 7 states it, and the cheapest correct place for this one probe is the next skills(B) round's batch, which already pays the per-sweep overhead. The four cases (bnbw-near/mid/far + one negative) are in skills/trigger-cases.json and are ready to run as-is.

measured-exemption.why: Written by round 359 (SWE-loop D). Same reasoning as bounded-not-binary-witness above: a probe is a priced live run, and the cheapest correct place for one is the next skills(B) batch, which already pays the per-sweep overhead. Four cases (three positive, one negative) ARE authored, by round 359 -- the same round that wrote the description, which is exactly the paraphrase-leak shape round 357's item 3 names as undetectable from the text. Recorded here rather than hidden: when this skill is probed, its per-case result is weaker evidence than a case written by a different round would be.

measured-not-declared-dependencies.why: Written by round 361 (harness A). Same standing convention as bounded-not-binary-witness / measured-exemption / refusal-set-differential above: a probe is a priced live run and a non-skills(B) round does not launch one for a single skill -- the per-sweep overhead belongs to a batch. NO trigger cases are authored yet, deliberately: round 357 item 3 names the paraphrase-leak shape where the round that writes the description also writes the cases, and this round chose to leave the cases to the batch round rather than add a fourth instance of it. That makes this skill WEAKER evidence than the others until cases exist, and it is recorded here rather than hidden.

refusal-set-differential.why: Written by round 360 (language C). A probe is a priced live run and this program's standing convention (round 334 item 7, applied by round 358 and round 359) is that a round which is not skills(B) does not launch one for a single skill -- the per-sweep overhead belongs to a batch. Four cases (rsd-near/mid/far plus one negative) are in skills/trigger-cases.json. They were authored by the round that wrote the description, which is round 357 item 3's paraphrase-leak shape; they deliberately avoid the description's own nouns ("refusal set", "differential", "mirror") and use a Rust/Python port, a JS/Go pair and an error-record-vs-raise framing instead, but that is mitigation, not independence.
